title: Deployment security evidence kit and SIEM export playbook
body:
Purpose:
This is a pragmatic playbook for packaging release security evidence, validating RBAC v2 mappings, and ensuring SIEM export readiness before any production deployment or capacity change. Focused on the 1–3 day prelaunch window for Hosted/Dedicated/Private releases.

Quick TL;DR checklist (start here):
- [ ] Evidence bundle created (S3 path) + ephemeral access token created and attached to release ticket
- [ ] RBAC v2 mapping validated against service-account matrix for the release scope
- [ ] Audit log schema validated for events with sample export to SIEM staging
- [ ] Exception requests filed for any dev/prod permission gaps (see exception flow)
- [ ] Sign-offs collected (Security, SRE, Product, Release Manager) using the sign-off stub below

1) Evidence bundle contents (packaging standard)
- metadata.json (release_id, commit_sha, owner, environment, windows_of_change)
- rbac-snapshot.csv (role, principal, resources, allow/deny, explanation)
- audit-sample.log (10–50 lines of representative events covering authN/authZ, token lifecycle, role changes, elevated requests)
- siem-export-config.yml (fields-to-export, field-mappings, timestamp-format)
- kms-manifest.txt (KMS key ids used to encrypt artifacts)
- ci-run-links.txt (links to CI artifacts: infra tests, e2e, canary results)
- manual-checks.md (freeform reviewer notes + open questions)

Storage convention: s3://redwood-release-evidence/{release_id}/{bundle_version}/. Use lifecycle 90d and set bucket encryption & access logging on.

2) RBAC v2 validation steps (fast path)
- Export current RBAC policy: tools/rbac-export --env prod --out rbac-snapshot.csv
- Compare with expected matrix (product team provides expected_roles.csv)
- Flag mismatches: any principal with broader permission than expected -> create exception request or revert to canary-only rollout
- Quick mapping table (example lines to include in rbac-snapshot.csv):
  role,principal,resource,verbs,notes
  inference.reader,svc-token-runner,projects/*/models/*,get,list,used by monitoring
  inference.invoker,team-deploy-bot,projects/*/models/*,create,run,for canary deploys only

Notes: RBAC v2 changes must include a migration plan entry (who has the old role, who will be removed and when).

3) Audit log schema sanity checks
- Minimum required fields: timestamp, event_type, principal_id, principal_type, resource, action, request_id, outcome, origin_ip, agent
- Recommended enrichment: model_version, sequence_id, kv_cache_hit, route_decision
- Validate with sample: curl -s -X POST https://siem-staging.redwood.internal/api/ingest -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d @audit-sample.log
- Confirm 1) timestamps parse correctly, 2) outcome values map to SIEM severity rules

4) SIEM export config example (siem-export-config.yml snippet)
fields_to_export:
  - timestamp
  - principal_id
  - event_type
  - resource
  - outcome
  - model_version
field_mappings:
  timestamp: ts
  principal_id: user.id
  event_type: type
  resource: target
timestamp_format: iso8601
batch_window_seconds: 30

Operational check: run the export pipeline in dry-run and verify counts and schema in SIEM index (index: redwood-audit-{env}-YYYY.MM.DD).

5) Exception approval and routing flow (when RBAC mismatch or missing evidence)
- Step 1: Owner files exception ticket with rationale, duration, mitigation and attached evidence bundle. Label: security-exception/{release_id}
- Step 2: Auto-notify: #sec-exceptions (Slack), security-oncall@redwood.com, and release manager
- Step 3: Triage within 4 business hours. If low-risk and time-critical, security can issue 24–72h fast-track approval with compensating controls (e.g., tighter network ACLs, increased audit sampling).
- Step 4: If high-risk (write/delete on sensitive resources, or KMS key exposures), require SRE + Security + Engineering manager sign-off and documented rollout rollback plan. No exceptions >72h without exec approval.

Escalation matrix (examples):
- Tier 1 (fast-track): Rina Okafor (security), @sec-fasttrack slack, approval window 24–72h
- Tier 2 (high-risk): Jon Bishop (SRE), Miguel Torres (product infra), approval required within 24h for emergency rollback
- Exec (permanent exception >72h): Head of Security + VP Eng sign-off

6) Sign-off stub (copy into ticket and attach):
---SIGN-OFF STUB---
Release: {release_id}
Owner: {owner}
Environment: {env}
Bundle path: s3://redwood-release-evidence/{release_id}/{bundle_version}/
RBAC deviations: yes/no (list brief)
SIEM export tested: yes/no (index sample: {index})
Exception filed: ticket #{id} or none
Approvals: Security: {name, date}, SRE: {name, date}, Product: {name, date}, Release mgr: {name, date}
---END STUB---

7) Automation pointers (tickets & scripts)
- Tools to generate bundle: scripts/evidence/pack_release_evidence.sh {release_id} -> outputs tar.gz + metadata.json
- Jenkins job: release-evidence-packager (params: release_id, env, bundle_version)
- CI hook: when release is tagged, auto-run rbac-export and audit-sample collection into temp artifact store (for review only)
- TODO: add a Lambda to push artifact summary into Jira ticket automatically (low effort, high value)

8) Reviewer guidance and red flags
- Red flag: audit samples show admin role changes without concurrent PR/written change
- Red flag: SIEM dry-run drops >5% of events or timestamp mismatch across more than 1 minute
- Red flag: KMS manifests referencing keys with no rotation schedule or external owners

9) After-release follow-up
- Keep evidence bundle for minimum 90 days; move to long-term archive on 1yr retention after that
- If exception was used, add retrospective note in ticket and schedule a KB item to remove exception by deadline

Appendix (links & snippets):
- Confluence runbook: CONFLUENCE-SEC-1234 (policy details)
- Jira template: JIRA-OPS-8890 (exception request)
- Example curl for SIEM ingest: curl -XPOST https://siem-staging.redwood.internal/api/ingest -H 'Authorization: Bearer ${SIEM_KEY}' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' --data-binary @audit-sample.log

Notes to self: add quick-check script for timestamp drift and a small dashboard tile in Console for "recent export failures". Also, sync with DevRel about documenting the RBAC roles for partner integrators.

Document history: created 2025-11-04 by Asha Patel. Drafted and shared with sec & SRE for feedback 2026-01-15. Last modified to add SIEM mapping and escalation matrix 2026-03-01.
